_meta.indication: ADDYI is indicated for the treatment of premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) characterized by low sexual desire causing marked distress or interpersonal difficulty; not indicated in postmenopausal women or men, or to enhance sexual performance
_meta.receipt_date: February 18, 2015 (complete response resubmission; original NDA dated and received October 27, 2009)

pivotal_trials.population: Premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD of at least 6 months duration
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Two co-primary endpoints: change from baseline to Week 24 in monthly satisfying sexual events (SSEs) and in eDiary sexual desire score
pivotal_trials.n: flibanserin 100 mg qhs (290), flibanserin 50 mg qhs (295), placebo (295)
pivotal_trials.result: SSE met (median treatment difference 1.0; p<0.01); but eDiary desire co-primary failed (treatment diff 2.3 [95% CI -0.1, 4.7]; NS)

nct_ctgov.title: 24-week Placebo-controlled Trial of Flibanserin Once Daily in Premenopausal Women With Hypoactive Sexual Desire Disorder

pivotal_trials.population: Premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD of at least 6 months duration
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline to Week 24 in monthly SSEs and in eDiary sexual desire score
pivotal_trials.n: 365 ADDYI vs 372 placebo (full analysis set); among randomized arms flibanserin 25 mg bid (396), flibanserin 50 mg qhs then 50 mg bid (392)
pivotal_trials.result: SSE met (median treatment difference 0.5; p<0.01); eDiary desire co-primary failed (treatment diff 1.7 [95% CI -0.5, 4.0]; NS)

nct_ctgov.title: Uptitration Trial of Flibanserin Versus Placebo in Premenopausal Women With Hypoactive Sexual Desire Disorder

pivotal_trials.population: Premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD of at least 6 months duration
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline to Week 24 in monthly SSEs and in FSFI Desire domain score
pivotal_trials.result: Both co-primaries met: SSE median treatment difference 0.5 (p<0.0001); FSFI Desire treatment difference 0.3 (95% CI 0.2, 0.4; p<0.0001)

nct_ctgov.title: Fixed 100 mg Every Evening of Flibanserin vs Placebo in Premenopausal Women With Hypoactive Sexual Desire Disorder

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥2%) were dizziness (11.4% vs 2.2% placebo), somnolence (11.2% vs 2.9%), nausea (10.4% vs 3.9%), fatigue (9.2% vs 5.5%), insomnia (4.9% vs 2.8%), and dry mouth (2.4% vs 1.0%); serious risks include severe hypotension and syncope, especially with alcohol or CYP3A4 inhibitors, and CNS depression
target_moa: Mechanism in HSDD is unknown; flibanserin has high affinity as an agonist at 5-HT1A and antagonist at 5-HT2A, with moderate antagonist activity at 5-HT2B, 5-HT2C, and dopamine D4 receptors

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: HYPOTENSION AND SYNCOPE IN CERTAIN SETTINGS — use with alcohol is contraindicated due to risk of severe hypotension and syncope; ADDYI is available only through the ADDYI REMS Program; also contraindicated with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and in hepatic impairment

rems.type: ADDYI is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the ADDYI REMS Program, due to the risk of severe hypotension and syncope from an alcohol interaction; prescribers and pharmacies must be certified

advisory_committee.vote: Joint Bone, Reproductive and Urologic Drugs AC and Drug Safety and Risk Management AC met June 4, 2015; of 24 voting members, 18 voted the benefit/risk acceptable to support approval only if risk management beyond labeling is implemented and 6 voted against

description.text: Expanded indication to include women less than 65 years of age independent of reproductive status

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for extending the indication to include women less than 65 years of age independent of reproductive status.

summary.text: Flibanserin, a new molecular entity, was approved under section 505(b) in its third review cycle after two prior Complete Response letters; approval was based on three Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled trials and was accompanied by a boxed warning, an ETASU REMS, and multiple required postmarketing studies, following a June 4, 2015 advisory committee that supported approval with risk management beyond labeling

citations.quote: This is the third review cycle for flibanserin (tradename Addyi), a new molecular entity proposed for the treatment of hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women. Flibanserin is a high affinity 5-hydroxytryptamine (HT)1A receptor agonist and 5-HT2A receptor antagonist, and a moderate antagonist at the 5-HT2B, 5-HT2C, and dopamine D4 receptors.
